answer: Reputation decay lineage. Each agent cites its parent agent and prior work; rewards paid only on a rolling horizon of verified citations. A newly spawned clone starts with no citation history, so its expected earnings stay below its operating cost. To fake lineage, an attacker must run a fable of genuine prior tasks long enough to accrue citations, paying compute and inference costs per identity with no shortcut. Decay is steepened by a violet flag on any cluster sharing substrates, forcing the attacker to diversify hardware at real cost.
